title: An Introduction to Large Language Models for Scientists and Professionals
abstract: arXiv:2610.37684v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have rapidly become important tools for science, education, medicine, and professional work. Despite their apparent simplicity from the user's perspective, effective and responsible use requires an understanding of how these systems work, what their limitations are, and how their outputs should be evaluated. I wrote this document as a basis for my lecture on LLM in the master in artificial intelligence in medicine at the university of Turin, Italy. This book provides a practical and accessible introduction to LLMs for scientists and professionals. It explains the fundamental ideas behind tokenisation, embeddings, training, inference, context windows, prompting, and instruction hierarchies, while deliberately avoiding mathematical detail. translated_title: 面向科学家与专业人士的大语言模型导论
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLMs）已迅速成为科学、教育、医学和专业工作中的重要工具。尽管从用户的角度来看它们看似简单，但要有效且负责任地使用这些系统，需要了解它们的工作原理、局限性以及应如何评估其输出结果。作者撰写本文档是作为其在意大利都灵大学医学人工智能硕士课程中大语言模型讲座的基础。本书为科学家和专业人士提供了实用且易于理解的大语言模型入门介绍，解释了分词、嵌入、训练、推理、上下文窗口、提示工程和指令层次结构背后的基本思想，同时有意避免过多的数学细节。书中特别关注了大语言模型生成答案的局限性，包括幻觉、不确定性、可重复性、偏见以及对系统性验证的需要。
tldr: 本书为科学家和专业人士提供了一本实用易懂的大语言模型入门读物，在避免复杂数学细节的前提下讲解LLM的核心概念，并重点剖析了其输出结果的局限性（如幻觉、不确定性和偏见）。
en_tdlr: This book offers scientists and professionals a practical, accessible introduction to large language models, explaining core concepts without mathematical detail while focusing on the limitations of LLM outputs such as hallucinations, uncertainty, and bias.
